summary.text: Jamie Raskin is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 8th Congressional District, which he has represented since 2017. A constitutional law professor for more than 25 years and a three-term Maryland state senator before Congress, he is the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee.

paragraphs.text: Raskin was born in Washington, D.C., and graduated from Georgetown Day School in 1979.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Harvard College in 1983 and a law degree from Harvard Law School in 1987, where he was an editor of the Harvard Law Review.

After law school, Raskin worked for two years as an assistant attorney general in the Massachusetts Attorney General's Office, and in 1989-1990 he served as general counsel of the National Rainbow Coalition.

In 1990 he began teaching constitutional law at American University's Washington College of Law, where he co-founded and directed an LL.M. program on law and government and co-founded the Marshall-Brennan Constitutional Literacy Project.
Raskin was elected to the Maryland Senate (District 20, Montgomery County) in 2006 and served from 2007 to 2017; his colleagues chose him as Senate Majority Whip.
His state legislative work included sponsoring the first National Popular Vote bill in the country and a benefit corporation law.
Raskin won the Democratic primary in 2016 for the open seat vacated by Chris Van Hollen and was elected to Congress that November. He was sworn into his fifth term in January 2025.

In the 119th Congress he is ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee. Earlier, he was lead impeachment manager in the second impeachment trial of President Donald Trump in 2021 and served on the Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack on the United States Capitol.

He is the author of Unthinkable: Trauma, Truth and the Trials of American Democracy, Overruling Democracy: The Supreme Court versus the American People, and We the Students: Supreme Court Cases for and About America's Students.
